headline: Medium-risk pair: OpenBBTerminal can ingest financial files while pdf.js renders PDFs, creating shared-content injection and data-handling risks; no direct evidence of dangerous defaults.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and APIs, and pdf.js processes PDF files in a browser-based worker model. If OpenBBTerminal consumes PDF-derived text or shared files from pdf.js without provenance checks, attacker-controlled document content can steer downstream prompts or actions. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal ingests text extracted from PDFs rendered by pdf.js without provenance filtering, injection is plausible.
IF the two agents share a workspace or file handoff path, document content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Require explicit provenance tags on all pdf.js-derived text.
Insert a manual review step before OpenBBTerminal acts on PDF content.
Restrict shared folders to read-only for pdf.js outputs.
Use allowlisted prompt templates for any MCP-fed content.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data, while pdf.js handles PDF documents. Even though both show no network egress, a shared workspace or file exchange could expose sensitive financial material from OpenBBTerminal into PDF workflows or vice versa. The profiles do not prove isolation, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or mounted workspace, file contents can leak across the boundary.
IF OpenBBTerminal exports financial data into PDFs processed by pdf.js, sensitive data may be exposed in rendered outputs.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Disable automatic export of financial data into shared PDF locations.
Use per-agent service accounts and distinct storage roots.
Review file permissions on any shared mount.
requires-engineering: add DLP controls for shared document flows.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and APIs, while pdf.js is a browser-based worker with PDF-file I/O. There is no evidence of overlapping write access to the same mutable resource, git state, or shared OAuth scopes. A conflict is possible only if an external orchestrator gives them the same writable target, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF shared mutable resources are introduced later, coordination issues may appear.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Keep pdf.js outputs read-only.
Avoid shared OAuth scopes.
Serialize writes in the orchestrator.
requires-engineering: add locking for any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenBBTerminal can consume APIs and MCP inputs, and pdf.js can produce rendered or extracted document content. If OpenBBTerminal treats pdf.js output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations in the document layer can cascade into financial analysis or actions. The interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is forwarded into OpenBBTerminal without verification, downstream decisions may inherit errors.
IF OpenBBTerminal automates analysis from document text, a bad PDF parse can propagate.
mitigations: Require source-document verification before action.
Compare extracted text against the original PDF for critical fields.
Add a human approval step for financial outputs.
Log provenance from pdf.js to OpenBBTerminal.
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating on document-derived inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, while pdf.js handles PDF documents. If financial or licensed material is rendered or stored as PDFs, retention and residency policies can diverge across the pair. No specific certification mismatch is documented, so this is a medium compliance-risk inference rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated financial documents are processed through pdf.js, retention rules may differ from OpenBBTerminal's handling.
IF the deployment stores PDFs in a different jurisdiction or retention tier than financial data, compliance drift occurs.
mitigations: Classify financial PDFs before processing.
Align retention settings across both agents.
Keep regulated documents in a single jurisdictional store.
Review secret-handling paths for OpenBBTerminal.
requires-engineering: map data-class policies to each storage location.
